content.title: Alabama's Jonathan Young is back for 'Survivor 50' after a near-win
content.text: Feb. 23, 2026, 11:36 a.m. CTAs Survivor marks an unprecedented milestone with its 50th season, one Alabama competitor from recent years is heading back to the island, determined to turn his near-miss into victory.fcJonathan Young, who first captured fans’ attention on Survivor 42, is among the 24 returning castaways competing in Survivor 50: In the Hands of the Fans, which premieres Wednesday, Feb. 25, on CBS and Paramount +.Here’s what to know about Young and his journey back to Survivor.Who is Jonathan Young?Young, hailing from Gulf Shores, made a name for himself on Survivor 42, where he placed fourth after 25 days of grueling competition. A former University of Alabama swimmer and lifelong beach enthusiast, Young owns a beach rental business in his hometown, and he’s said running it has been a training ground for the ultimate challenge. His journey to Survivor started young. At 14, he competed on Endurance, a kids’ version of Survivor. He got a taste of what the show would be like and wanted to do the real thing. Young’s time on Survivor 42On Survivor 42, Young was a member of the Taku tribe and was immediately identified as a physical threat. He consistently performed in tribe challenges, at times completing tasks that other tribes abandoned. Young ultimately fell short in the fire-making challenge, missing a spot in the finale. He reached the final four and finished in fourth place.What to know about Survivor 50Survivor 50: In the Hands of the Fans will celebrate the long-running reality show’s 50th season. For the first time, fans voted on key game elements, from tribe colors to challenges, giving the season a fresh twist. The cast features 24 returning players, including past winners and fan favorites, competing in Fiji for the $1 million prize. With classic alliances, brutal physical challenges and unpredictable Tribal Councils, the milestone season promises intense competition and plenty of surprises.Jennifer Lindahl is a Breaking and Trending Reporter for the Deep South Connect Team for USA Today. Connect with her on X @jenn_lindahl and email at jlindahl@usatodayco.com.
